newsitem.title: INDIA: India to reconsider cellular phone tariff rates.
newsitem.headline: India to reconsider cellular phone tariff rates.

text.p: India's Telecommunications Minister Beni Prasad Verma said on Thursday the government will reconsider requests of cellular telephone operators on high tariff rates for calls from basic, fixed-line phones to mobile units.

Verma has asked the Telecom Commission "to make a detailed examination of the representations received from the mobile service operators on call charges and give its recommendations," a ministry statement said.
Cellular telephone operators asked an Indian court on Tuesday to overturn a government order which they said set prohibitively high tariff rates for calls from basic telephones to mobile units.

G.P. Sangal, a spokesman for the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI), said on Tuesday the trade group filed a petition with the Delhi High Court challenging the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) order.
The January 29 order set tariff rates which Sangal said were far higher than warranted except in the four largest cities -- Bombay, Calcutta, Delhi and Madras.
Cellular operators, admitted under an economic liberalisation programme, launched their services in 1995, starting with the four "metropolitan" cities.
The high court on Tuesday rejected the cellular operators' request for a stay on the order, due to take effect on Saturday, and set a hearing for April 3 on COAI's plea.

Sangal said that under the rates set by the order, a phone call from a basic phone to a cellular unit within the same area, or circle, would cost the user of the basic phone about 10 rupees a minute compared with the current 1.4 rupees.
Normal fixed-line charges would remain in force in the four largest cities.
